first_impression.reaction: My daughter sent this, so I read it properly, start to finish, on the iPad. The opening is a bit flowery for me ('a month of edges'), but it gets to the point quickly: Europe is closing up, the islands are starting their rains. That is useful to know before anyone pays a deposit. No silly slang, which I appreciate. There are a lot of temperature and rainfall numbers, though. I skimmed those. What I was really looking for was who is responsible, what happens to our money, and how my mother will cope. Some of that is here, not all of it.

journey.quote: For couples weighing wedding destinations, November is a month of edges.
journey.reaction: A bit poetic. Fine, but I would rather be told plainly what November is like.

journey.section: How we chose these ten November destinations
journey.quote: Base periods and the way a rain day is counted differ from country to country, and the [WMO asks for care when city climates are set side by side](https://worldweather.wmo.int/en/city.html?cityId=604), so read each figure on its own.
journey.reaction: I had to read this twice. I don't know what a base period is. It sounds careful and honest, but it is written for a meteorologist, not for me.

journey.quote: The [Hellenic National Meteorological Service's figures for Naxos](http://oldportal.emy.gr/emy/en/climatology/climatology_city?perifereia=South%20Aegean&poli=Naxos), for which HNMS publishes no base period, give a November minimum monthly temperature of 13.7°C, a monthly mean of 16.4°C and a maximum of 18.8°C.
journey.reaction: Too many numbers in one sentence. Each destination has a paragraph like this and they blur together. I'd skip to the questions underneath, which are the useful part.

journey.quote: Which ferries still run that week, and what is the plan if a crossing is cancelled?
journey.reaction: Good. That is exactly what I would worry about with older relatives on an island.

journey.quote: Lemon terraces without the summer traffic, in the wettest month on the nearby Naples table, on a coast of open terraces and stairs.
journey.reaction: Stairs. My mother uses a walking frame. I'm glad they said it honestly, but now I want to know whether there is any way in without steps, and the page doesn't say.

journey.quote: How do guests reach the terrace from the road in heavy rain, and is there a covered route?
journey.reaction: Sensible question, and the sort I'd be made to feel fussy for asking. Nice to see it written down.

journey.quote: Can the ceremony move under cover at an hour's notice, and who decides?
journey.reaction: 'Who decides' is the right question. Someone has to be responsible on the day.

journey.quote: If a cyclone closes the airport that week, what happens to the date and the rooms?
journey.reaction: Frankly this alarms me a little, but I'd rather know. It doesn't go on to say what happens to the money we've already paid, which is my next question.

journey.quote: Will the resort put its wet weather and cyclone plans for the wedding in writing before we sign?
journey.reaction: In writing, before we sign. That is how I like things done.

journey.section: Wet and cyclone seasons in November
journey.quote: Read the terms for a date moved by a cyclone, and check that travel insurance covers it, as Smartraveller suggests for Mauritius.
journey.reaction: Insurance and Smartraveller mentioned, good, those are things I recognise. Still nothing about whether deposits are protected if the date moves.

journey.section: Venues at the end of the European season
journey.quote: Ask each one, in writing, whether it is open on your date and which rooms are heated.
journey.reaction: Fine, but if it's an Italian or French venue, will the contract be in English, and what currency are we paying in? That isn't covered for the venue side.

journey.quote: Ask each venue whether a local public holiday falls near your date, and how guests who walk slowly manage wet steps.
journey.reaction: At least someone has thought of the older guests. It's one line, though. I'd want to know about step-free access and how far the nearest hospital or doctor is.

journey.quote: A Wedded Advisor works in your time zone, quotes in AUD and confirms each venue's inclusions in writing before you commit.
journey.reaction: This is the sentence that made me sit up. Australian dollars, in writing, someone in our time zone. I'd read that bit out to my husband.

journey.section: Plan your November wedding with Wedded Concierge
journey.quote: Your Wedded Advisor is your single point of contact for the venue, travel, vendors and payments, anywhere in the world, and the fee is agreed in writing before any work begins.
journey.reaction: One person, fee agreed in writing. Good. But who do I ring if something goes wrong at 2am Italian time, when we're actually there? 'Works in your time zone' is lovely before the trip, less so during it.

journey.section: Plan your November wedding with Wedded Concierge
journey.quote: Tell us your November date, your guest numbers and who will need extra care on the journey through [Wedded Concierge](/wonderland-concierge?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=wedding-destinations-november&utm_content=closing).
journey.reaction: 'Who will need extra care on the journey' made me feel they understand families like ours. I don't know whether filling this in means someone phones me, though, and I would want a phone call before anything is booked.

unanswered_questions: Is the deposit protected? What happens to money already paid if a cyclone or venue closure moves the date?
Who do I ring if something goes wrong at 2am local time while we are overseas?
Will I get to speak to a real person on the phone before anything is booked, and who is that person?
Are overseas venue contracts in English, and in which currency are the venue and suppliers actually paid?
Can someone with a walking frame get to the ceremony and reception at these places, and is there step-free access?
How far is medical help from these venues, especially on the islands?
Who holds the money between us and the venue: is it paid through the Wedded Advisor or directly?

turn_offs_found.quote: The same table shows 52.3 mm of precipitation over 8.8 precipitation days, with the wind prevailing from the north.
turn_offs_found.why: The weather paragraphs are dense with figures and agency names. Not tiny grey text, but heavy reading on an iPad, and I don't need millimetres of rain to make a decision.

turn_offs_found.quote: Base periods and the way a rain day is counted differ from country to country, and the [WMO asks for care when city climates are set side by side](https://worldweather.wmo.int/en/city.html?cityId=604), so read each figure on its own.
turn_offs_found.why: Technical caveat that leaves me unsure what to do with all the numbers.

would_share_with: My husband, with the Fiji and Mauritius cyclone lines and the Wedded Advisor paragraph highlighted
My daughter, to ask which of these places her grandmother could manage

cta_reaction.quote: Tell us your November date, your guest numbers and who will need extra care on the journey through [Wedded Concierge](/wonderland-concierge?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=wedding-destinations-november&utm_content=closing).
cta_reaction.why: I like that it asks about guests who need extra care, and the fee in writing and AUD quotes reassure me. But I'd talk to my husband first, and I'd only go ahead if I knew a person would ring me and that our deposits are looked after. The page doesn't tell me either.

top_3_changes: Say what happens to deposits already paid if a cyclone or closure moves the date, at least as a question to put to the venue.
Give older and less mobile guests more than one line: step-free access and distance to medical help as questions for each venue.
Tell me to ask for venue contracts in English with the currency of every payment stated, so I'm not signing something I can't read.

suggested_edits.old: Read the terms for a date moved by a cyclone, and check that travel insurance covers it, as Smartraveller suggests for Mauritius.
suggested_edits.new: Read the terms for a date moved by a cyclone, including what happens to deposits already paid, and check that travel insurance covers it, as Smartraveller suggests for Mauritius.
suggested_edits.why: My biggest fear is deposits disappearing. This adds the question without claiming anything about the brand.

suggested_edits.old: Ask each venue whether a local public holiday falls near your date, and how guests who walk slowly manage wet steps.
suggested_edits.new: Ask each venue whether a local public holiday falls near your date, how guests who walk slowly manage wet steps, whether there is a step-free way in, and how far the nearest doctor or hospital is.
suggested_edits.why: My mother uses a walking frame. These are the two things I'd ask first.

suggested_edits.old: Ask each one, in writing, whether it is open on your date and which rooms are heated.
suggested_edits.new: Ask each one, in writing, whether it is open on your date and which rooms are heated, and ask for the contract in English with the currency of every payment stated.
suggested_edits.why: Contracts in another language and currency worry me. This is a question to ask, not a claim.

checks.check: Every journey point, turn-off and CTA reaction quotes an exact sentence from 05-draft.md
Stayed in character as Margaret (funding parent, 62, reading on iPad)
No invented brand facts; unknowns (phone call, deposit protection, after-hours contact) listed as unanswered questions
HTML comments and [[VERIFY]] markers treated as invisible
Suggested edits are exact old/new strings, at most 3, and add no prices, venue names, statistics, business details or new weather facts
Scores are 1 to 5 for all five required dimensions

assumptions: Persona is provisional and not CRM-calibrated, so reactions reflect the card only.
Margaret arrived via a link her daughter sent and read top to bottom on an iPad, per the persona card.
task_id was not supplied by the orchestrator and was constructed from the slug, stage and persona.

open_questions.question: Can the page state whether a Wedded Advisor is reachable during the trip (after hours, local time), and whether an enquiry leads to a phone call? Only if Wedded Wonderland confirms it; I have not suggested wording because it would be a business detail.
Is there an approved line on how client payments and deposits are handled or protected? Funding parents will look for it.
